newsitem.title: UK: Princess Diana denies rift over blood sports.
newsitem.headline: Princess Diana denies rift over blood sports.

text.p: Britain's Princess Diana denied on Sunday that she is worried about her son William's interest in blood sports after news broke that he had shot his first stag.
"Both the princess and Prince William have a very close relationship and she respects that he has interests in every arena and would not question them," she said in a statement.
Diana, who was divorced from Britain's heir-to-the-throne Prince Charles in August, issued the statement after the Sunday Mirror newspaper reported she was sickened by her son's interest in hunting.
"Diana: My fear for gun-crazed Wills" the paper said in a front-page story.
It said Diana feared her eldest son would turn into "a remorseless hunter with a blood-lust" after his first kill.
"The animal-loving princess is deeply concerned about the psychological effects that hunting -- so favoured by the royals -- will have on princes William and Harry," it said.
Without naming any specific newspaper, Diana said one front-page story was "cruel in its inaccuracies".

William is reported to have stalked and shot his first stag last month on Queen Elizabeth's Balmoral estate in the Scottish Highlands. The 14-year-old prince reportedly made the kill in the company of his 12-year-old brother Harry and Prince Charles.
Charles is a keen hunter, as is Tiggy Legge-Bourke, the aide who looks after the boys when they are with their father.
"In a stern warning from Buckingham Palace, the princess has been told that their pastime is none of her business and she must not speak out," the Sunday Mirror said.
It said Prince William enjoys hunting so much he may get his own shotgun for Christmas.
